utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The late start is to some extent, also due to the fact that the statement we asked for was not received during the weekend but was only here this morning, which surprised us because the Defence took great effort putting a lot of statements not related to witness number one, but to what seemed to have bothered them more than what the Chamber asked for. I would like to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. When we were in private session, the Chamber has dealt with procedural aspects in relation to an application for protective measures for the next witness, Witness P-001. The Chamber goes beyond what was asked, the parties agreeing on this, and decides that the testimony of Witness P-001 will be heard in closed session, reasons to be given orally in due course. We turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Lyntton.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lyntton, before you give evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration, that you will speak the truth the whole truth and nothing but the truth. May I invite to you make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lyntton. Please be seated. Mr. Lyntton you will now be examined by Mr. Margetts, who is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Good morning. Could you please state your full name for the record?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON
utterances.text: Richard Lyntton.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Lyntton, did you give a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor on the 3rd of October, 2001?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Registrar, if 65 ter 5442 could be brought up on the screen, please. Mr. Lyntton, if you can look at the left-hand side of the screen there is that the statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Now, if we can turn a page, please, Mr. Registrar, and you'll see, Mr. Lyntton, that on the side of the statement there are handwritten annotations marking the numbers of the paragraphs. Now, since you have been in the in The Hague have you had an opportunity to review the statement you gave and have you noted that those handwritten annotations have been inserted by the Office of the Prosecutor in the statement?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And apart from those handwritten annotations this is the statement that you gave on the 3rd of October, 2001?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, since have you been in The Hague, have you had a chance to review that statement and were there any corrections that you would like to make to that statement?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON
utterances.text: I have and there were some corrections.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And if I may, Mr. Registrar, if we could move to page 3 of the statement, and to paragraph 14 of the statement. You will see in line 3 of paragraph 14, Mr. Lyntton, you refer to a group of new white mini-buses. Since you have been in The Hague, have you been given the opportunity to review a video of the event that is described in paragraph 14?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And are there any corrections you would like it make to that reference?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And what are they?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON
utterances.text: There were in fact six vehicles, three -- three blue jeeps and three white jeeps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lyntton.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: If we could now move on page 5, please, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Now, on this page of your statement, you will see that from paragraphs 26 through paragraph 31, you refer to an interview that you conducted with General Cermak. At the bottom of the screen --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Registrar, if we could scroll down a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: You'll see there's a reference there to August 26th, 1995. Now, the implication being that the events under that reference occurred on August the 26th, 1995. Could you clarify with the Court whether on what day the events that are described in paragraphs 26 to 31 occurred?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON
utterances.text: The interview with General Cermak actually took place on the 26th and not the 25th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could now move to paragraph 29 that can you see in the middle of the screen. There's a reference to the interview, beginning at around 1600 hours. Is that correct or did the interview in fact begin on the 26th at a different time.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON
utterances.text: It was a different time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And what was that time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON
utterances.text: It was -- I don't remember exactly but it was towards lunch-time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Around about midday?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON
utterances.text: Yeah. I would put it at about 11.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you. And there adjust -- I'm just pausing to allow for the French translation and the Croatian translation. If I could now refer you to paragraph 27, and in particular, the last sentence, wherein you state that you recall that Cermak said he would -- that we could ask the questions in English and he would reply in Croatian. Did you have the opportunity to review the video of the interview and is there any clarification that you'd like to give in relation to that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON
utterances.text: Yes. We -- I did review the interview, and around in fact we had -- we used an interpreter so I asked the English -- the questions in English and we used an interpreter to interpret my answer -- my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you. And apart from that does the October 2001 statement accurately reflect the content of the statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And would you give the same statement if you were asked the same questions today?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON
utterances.text: I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And the statement together with the corrections that you've made in court today is that true and accurate to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD LYNTTON
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. President, could the October 2001 statement please be given an exhibit number, and entered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number P870.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Therefore, P870 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, I believe you will have received in the last hour, and the parties as well, an updated exhibit list for this witness. There are six items apart from the ICTY statement on that exhibit list. I'd just like to clarify in respect of the last item. We had initially referenced and this is for the parties' reference as well. We had initially referenced the full transcript of raw footage of an interview with Edward Flynn. We're content that in fact the important components of that interview are covered by Exhibit P28, so we no longer wish to tender the full transcript of that interview with Mr. Flynn. The second clarification is that instead of introducing the full footage of the various videos that Mr. Lyntton shot, we have reduce the footage to the relevant sections and therefore we assigned new 65 ter numbers as you see in the left hand column. And the other clarification is that the parties will be aware that all of the items on this exhibit list were part of the 92 ter submission apart from the second item, which is the 65 ter 5463, that item has referenced in the witness's October 2001 statement just by a reference saying he took a video but didn't have the specific identification but this is a video referenced in paragraph 9 of his statement. And with those clarifications, Mr. President, I'd like to move the four documents that have not previously -- or the four videos and the transcripts that have not previously been moved into evidence, into evidence. If I have could exhibit numbers for each of those items.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are there any objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: No objections Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. The Chamber earlier raised the issue of whether we would admit very lengthy videos, hours and hours, this is more limited in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will admit the items even if not played in court. I don't know if you want to play portions of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. President, just some very small portion of one of the videos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, I think we started 5463, 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit number P871.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just heard the reference to 4563 that is what has come up in the transcript. I think it is 5463 was the first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's 5463. P870 [sic] is admitted into evidence. Next one, P5464, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, just to clarify, the last exhibit was 5463 and that was Exhibit P871.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm making two mistakes at the same time. It was P871 is admitted into evidence. Now the next one I leave it to you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is 65 ter 5464, that becomes Exhibit number P872.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence. Next one would be --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That becomes Exhibit number P873, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you and then the last one is P5466.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes exhibit number P874, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Yes. P873 and P874 are admitted into evidence as well. We have only limited time left, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two to three minutes. I don't know if there's anything you could deal with in such a short period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I just have the summary of the witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could read that and you have explained to -- to Mr. Lyntton what purpose it serves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: In August 1995, Mr. Lyntton was a television producer working for UN TV. He travelled to Knin in order to explore the story of the Serbs that stayed behind after Operation Storm. Upon arriving, he was informed that there would be a meeting between local residents in the Plavno valley and the local police chief. He accompanied the UN representative, Mr. Edward Flynn, to the Plavno valley on the morning of the 25th of August, 1995 to attend the proposed meeting. Whilst en route, he interviewed an elderly couple in the area of the Plavno valley who told him that special forces members had placed them by a wall and threatened to shoot them. The meeting in the Plavno valley did not proceed as scheduled, since the police chief did not arrive. At around 11.00 on the 25th of August, the witness observed large plumes of smoke arising across the valley, approximately three kilometres away. Together with his production team and Mr. Flynn, the witness proceeded to the source of the smoke which they soon discovered was Grubori village. After filming homes on fire and interviewing villagers, the witness returned to Knin where he sought to arrange an interview with General Cermak, whom he had been told was the military governor in charge of the area. Next morning, on the 26th of August, 1995, the witness returned to the village of Grubori, where he observed and videoed two corpses of elderly men, one who had been sought in the head and the other who had had his throat cut. The witness interviewed villagers in the course of this visit. He returned to Knin, and around 11.30 a.m., he conducted an interview with General Cermak. General Cermak denied that old people had been forced out of their homes, and he denied that anyone had been shot at close quarters in Grubori. He asserted that there had been anti-terrorist operations conducted in the area. In the afternoon following the interview, the witness arranged for the videotapes of the events in Grubori and the interview with General Cermak to be transported to Zagreb by helicopter, and he returned to Zagreb by road. That concludes the summary, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lyntton, it was very short today. I would like to instruct you not to speak with anyone about the testimony you have given already today and the testimony still to be given tomorrow, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.00 in Courtroom III. We stand adjourned and we resume on Tuesday, the 16th of September, in Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 16th day of September, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.
